cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty'); if echo "$cmd" | grep -qE '(^|[ ;&|`])git[[:space:]]+commit '; then branch=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null); if [ "$branch" = "main" ]; then printf 'BLOCKED: git commit on main is forbidden.

Recovery (no commits yet on main):
  git checkout -b feat/YYYY-MM-DD-name

Recovery (commits already on main, not yet pushed):
  git stash                                           # save uncommitted work
  git checkout -b feat/YYYY-MM-DD-name                 # branch carries the commits
  git checkout main                                    # back to main
  git reset --soft origin/main && git restore --staged .   # rewind without losing work
  git checkout feat/YYYY-MM-DD-name && git stash pop   # resume on feature branch

Never use git reset --hard. Full procedure: AGENTS.md > Workflow > Recovery.
' >&2; exit 2; fi; fi

cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty'); if echo "$cmd" | grep -qF 'crates.io/api' && echo "$cmd" | grep -qE '(^|[[:space:];|&(`$])(curl|wget)[[:space:]]' && ! echo "$cmd" | grep -qiE 'user-agent[[:space:]]*[:=]|--user-agent[[:space:]]' && ! echo "$cmd" | grep -qE '(^|[[:space:]])-[a-zA-Z]*A([[:space:]]|=|["'"'"'])'; then printf 'BLOCKED: crates.io API fetch with no User-Agent.

crates.io rejects UA-less requests with a JSON *error body*, so `jq -r ".crate.max_stable_version"` prints the literal `null` and exits 0 -- a fact-shaped non-answer, not data (AGENTS.md > Dependency Versions; ai-docs/dependency-versions.md > Failure mode).

Use:
  curl -sS -H "User-Agent: graphite-gp-agent (<contact-email>)" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name>" | jq -r ".crate.max_stable_version"

Any of these satisfies the check: a literal `User-Agent:` / `user-agent=` anywhere (so -H, -H"..", -sSH "..", --header all work), `--user-agent <v>`, or an -A-style flag (-A "v", -A'"'"'v'"'"', -sSA "v"). A null from any version lookup means the QUERY FAILED -- re-run without the jq filter and read the raw body.

This hook matches COMMAND TEXT, not shell semantics: it cannot tell a real fetch from a heredoc/sed that merely quotes one, so it fails closed on those. If that is what you are doing, put a User-Agent in the quoted text too, or write the file with the Write tool.
' >&2; exit 2; fi

Bash reports the LAST pipeline stage exit status, so tail/head always exits 0 -- a RED gate gets recorded as green. tail -N can also truncate away the "test result:" line you needed (AGENTS.md > Build & Test).

Use instead:
  cargo test --workspace > gate.log 2>&1 && echo GATE-GREEN || echo GATE-RED
  grep -E "test result:|^error" gate.log

Or prefix with: set -o pipefail;

This hook matches COMMAND TEXT, not shell semantics -- a string that merely quotes such a pipeline also matches. Rephrase it or use the Write tool.
' >&2; exit 2; fi
